message: test(scripts): the status gate states its grammar, reads every bullet, and claims only cardinality

edits.find:
* A section that may hold one entry cannot accumulate a log at all, which is the property the
 * closed list above already had for headings, applied one level down to the place all three
 * departed logs actually grew. It also refuses the staleness a ceiling cannot see: **Now** held six
 * entries and five described closed work, and two of the three under **Next in line** called
 * merged pull requests unmerged. The phase bullet was a second Now with a different name and the
 * longest half-life of anything in the file, so it is refused by name. See ADR-085.

* Issue #403 is that gate's own machinery rather than its policy. The section reader answered from
 * an arbitrary byte offset for a heading it could not find, a bare marker counted as an entry, and
 * the phase rule refused one formatting of the label rather than the label itself. A gate that
 * answers confidently from the wrong place is the defect this file exists to refuse, so the reader
 * is total, an entry has to state something, and the label is read where a label goes. See ADR-085.

edits.find:
/**
 * The forbidden bullet's label, in the label position and read case-insensitively.
 *
 * Optionally `current`, then `phase`, then the end of the label rather than more words: a colon, a
 * hyphen, an en dash, an em dash or nothing at all end it, because the spellings issue #403 found
 * use every one of them. Prose that mentions a phase further along a real entry is not a label and
 * is not refused, and this file's own **Open, and not scheduled** section relies on that.
 */
const PHASE_LABEL = /^(?:current\s+)?phase\s*(?:[:\u2013\u2014-]|$)/i;
edits.replace:
/**
 * The forbidden bullet's label, in the label position and read case-insensitively.
 *
 * Optionally `current`, then `phase`, then an optional numeric designator, then the end of the label
 * rather than more words. Prose that mentions a phase further along a real entry is not a label and
 * is not refused, and this file's own **Open, and not scheduled** section relies on that.
 *
 * Issue #422 is the two halves of that sentence an enumeration could not reach. `Phase 6:` was
 * allowed, because the number sat between the label and the colon the rule was looking for, so a
 * writer could satisfy the gate by numbering the phase they were already numbering; #384 exists
 * because a reminder was not enough, and a rule satisfied by numbering is a reminder again. And the
 * terminator was a list of four characters, so `Phase = live editing` and `Phase / live editing`
 * passed a rule whose own issue existed to lengthen that list. Any character that is neither a word
 * character nor whitespace ends the label now, which is the answer that stops the list from being
 * the thing maintained. Naming a closed set of terminators here instead is refused for that reason.
 *
 * The distinction the live file depends on survives both widenings, and it is the same one the rule
 * already drew without a number. `Phase 6 packaging follows the current phase.` is a real entry
 * under **Open, and not scheduled** and stays allowed, because no separator follows its designator.
 * The label is refused; the noun is not. See ADR-085.
 */
const PHASE_LABEL = /^(?:current\s+)?phase(?:\s*\d+)?\s*(?:[^\w\s]|$)/i;

edits.find: **Decision one. Now and Next in line carry exactly one entry each, and the gate counts them.** A section that may hold one entry cannot accumulate a log at all. That is the property the closed section list already had for headings, applied one level down to the entries inside a section the list allows, which is where every one of the three logs #284 removed actually grew. It also makes the rewrite rule enforceable rather than merely stated: an editor who has to delete the entry in front of them cannot quietly add one beside it, and what they delete is history that already lives in the pull request that landed it.

**Amendment, 2026-09-16: the reader states its grammar, the label rule reads every bullet, and a numbered label is refused.** [#421](https://github.com/chahyasantoso/motion5/issues/421), [#420](https://github.com/chahyasantoso/motion5/issues/420) and [#422](https://github.com/chahyasantoso/motion5/issues/422) sit in the same layer as the amendment above, and again no decision moves. The reader traded a byte offset for a line grammar narrower than Markdown and documented none of it, so it depended on Prettier for two thirds of that grammar while `core.autocrlf` was never a formatter question at all. One `statusLines` owner now strips carriage returns and trailing whitespace for every reader, so a Windows checkout and an unformatted heading are read rather than refused with a message about a section the file plainly has.

What the reader will not do is stated rather than assumed, and both refusals are recorded with their reasons. `*` and `+` are not recognised: one marker in one file is a contract worth defending, three markers is a parser a status file does not need, and Prettier normalises them before the gate reads them. A mixed-marker case is added anyway, because that is the one spelling that miscounts rather than refuses, and pinning it turns an invisible dependency into a written one. Fence awareness is likewise declined: an unindented section marker inside a fenced block is read as a real boundary, which produces a loud failure against the section list rather than a bypass, and this file has never had a fenced block.

The phase rule now reads every list bullet at any indent while the entry count stays top-level. Reusing one bullet set had carried the entry count's nested exemption to a question it was never argued for, so a phase bullet indented once under a real entry was refused by nothing and visible to everyone. Permitting a nested phase bullet is refused: the nested text is exactly as readable as the top-level one, so it recreates the stale second **Now** decision two removed. The label itself gains an optional numeric designator, so `Phase 6:` is refused while `Phase 6 packaging follows the current phase.` stays allowed, and its terminator becomes any character that is neither a word character nor whitespace rather than a list of four, because enumerating terminators is the list #422 exists to lengthen. Leading non-word characters are stripped before the match, so a decorated label is still a label while a link inside a sentence is not.
